narrative:
The model estimates a 64% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years was the strongest element pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expects to stay, only about half have this same limited experience level, while the rest tend to have six or more years. This signals to the model that you are still in an early career stage where people often explore other opportunities.

The fact that you have received other job offers while working here was the second most important factor, pushing the prediction strongly toward leaving. Most employees the model predicts will stay do not receive such external offers.

Your employment in the “other” sector, rather than medical or education, was the third notable influence and also nudged the outcome toward leaving. Only about 22% of employees expected to stay work in this broader category.

Although several positive elements in your situation, such as medium job support, medium emotional commitment, and no psychological exhaustion, pulled the prediction back toward staying, they were not strong enough to outweigh the top three factors.

The organization should discuss with you how to accelerate your development and address external opportunities. You may want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your longer-term goals.
